correctness.rationale: Proof uses object-intent inclusion and four-cycle locality to give |J-Jproxy|,|K-Kproxy|<=4Q+2 for all finite contexts. Exact tri-category probabilities yield both finite proxy expectations. The expected number of four-cycles is O(1) in the specified sparse regime. Row/column Efron–Stein with bounded squared degree effects gives O(n) proxy variances; these imply the joint L1 O(n^-1/2) law. Singleton-duplicate occupancy yields the positive discrepancy. Independent enumeration of 74,384 contexts, their duals, eight expectation identities and 1,500 further tests corroborates finite steps. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytic limit.

value.rationale: The number of distinct join/meet irreducible concepts is the intrinsic cardinality of the two sides of a canonical reduced representation, a natural data-reduction invariant. Two explicit densities, a uniform deterministic four-cycle stability bound, O(1) mean errors, quantitative L1 convergence, and a positive gap from individually indispensable input rows explain when separate deletions cannot be jointly combined. The theorem addresses a real structural/algorithmic issue, beyond a mere single small-table computation.
